summary.label: SUMMARY
summary.heading: I work out what to build before I build it.
body: Full-stack engineer with two years shipping production code at Programiz Pro, a coding-education platform with over 100,000 paid learners. I built the course flow and learner dashboard every paid learner works through, and the engine that issues their completion certificates. Most recently I led four engineers at Jobss.ai, where I owned authentication, role-based access and the employer workspace, and built the marketplace search both sides query — in Laravel.

During my Master's I built two connected systems from the data model up: a warehouse platform with lot-level inventory and state-machine fulfilment, and a multi-tenant Next.js storefront that trades stock with it. I work in React, Next.js, Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL and Laravel.

How I approach a project: I don't move quickly at the start. I ask questions that feel obvious until the answer turns out to be surprising, and I write code once I understand what it's supposed to do. I'm not the engineer who ships in week one and apologises in week four — I'm the one who's slower at the beginning and less painful at the end.
Originally from Nepal, now in Melbourne wrapping up a Master's in Software Engineering. Outside work I read, travel when I can, and watch more anime than is probably respectable.

entries.product: Job and task distribution platform. Laravel, PHP and Blade views built from Figma designs.
bullets: Led four engineers as technical lead — set the technical direction and ran code review. Nothing merged unread.
Owned authentication and the role-based access model that separates employers from job seekers, which every permission check in the rest of the platform reads from.
Designed the employer workspace end to end, so an employer posts a job or task and then moves applicants through review, shortlist and rejection without leaving it.
Built the marketplace search on a single index that serves both sides, so employers looking for people and seekers looking for work query the same system from opposite directions.
Chose cursor-based pagination over offset for the job and task feeds — read cost stays flat as the dataset grows rather than degrading with page depth, and the feed stays scoped to active dates.
Designed the allocation logic that spreads available workers across open jobs and tasks by demand, so no job sits unstaffed while another is oversubscribed.

entries.product: Coding-education platform — programiz.com and programiz.pro. Over 100,000 paid learners.
bullets: Led Programiz Reports, a feature for beginners learning to program, with a team of six on a Scrum cycle — gathered the requirements, owned the scope, ran sprint planning, and carried it from proposal to release.
Built the course flow and learner dashboard on programiz.pro, the surface all 100,000+ paid learners move through to finish a course.
Built the certificate engine that issues a verified completion certificate to every learner who finishes a course — over 100,000 issued so far.
Wrote end-to-end tests in Playwright and Cypress and ran them in a GitHub Actions CI workflow.
Worked on the in-browser Python and JavaScript compilers on programiz.com, where visitors run code without installing anything.
Integrated sensAI, the in-product tutor, so learners get help at the point in an exercise where they're stuck rather than after they give up.
Instrumented landing pages with Mixpanel and Microsoft Clarity, then rewrote the pages against what the behaviour data showed.

projects.label: PROJECTS
projects.heading: Systems I built end to end.

entries.name: Nexus — Warehouse Management Platform
entries.description: Personal project, built during my Master's after running an anime-apparel side business where stock went missing and fulfilment was manual. Trades stock and order state with Aroma.
bullets: Modelled the warehouse as a labelled tree — any item resolves to a location in seconds, which is the missing-stock problem the project was built to end.
Modelled product drops as a state machine covering supplier onboarding, lot negotiation, intake and lot-level pricing. Nothing advances out of order.
Recorded stock movements in a PostgreSQL ledger with SELECT FOR UPDATE row locks, so two buyers cannot claim one unit.
Built lot-aware replenishment with a return-to-order path, so a refund or exchange resolves back to the correct inventory state instead of drifting.
Wrote the fulfilment pipeline that batches retail orders on a timer and tracks each one to completion as its own state machine.

codeNote.text: Private repo — it runs a live side business, so the code isn't public. I'm happy to walk through the data model and the state machines.

entries.name: Aroma — Multi-tenant Clothing E-commerce
entries.description: Personal project. A multi-tenant storefront that trades stock with Nexus, so sellers run their own shop on shared infrastructure.
bullets: Designed the tenancy model so each seller runs an isolated storefront on one shared backend, drawing the line between what's shared and what a tenant controls.
Built the buyer path front to back: search and product pages through cart, reservation, checkout and order history.

Split rendering by page — server rendering and static generation for catalogue pages that have to be indexed and paint fast, client fetching for anything per-user, with React Query holding the cache and Zustand holding cart state.
Measured the product details page in Lighthouse rather than assuming it — Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) came in under two seconds.
Added a post-purchase order-status view. Sellers who trade only through social media can't offer that visibility, and the trust gap costs them sales.

codeNote.text: Private repo — pre-launch and connected to Nexus, so the code isn't public. I'm happy to walk through the tenancy model and the rendering split.

earlier.name: Hospital E-Ticketing
earlier.summary: A platform where hospitals and doctors register digitally, open weekly appointment slots, and patients book online — with an inversion-test algorithm that prevents double-bookings across Doctor, Patient and Hospital Admin roles.

earlier.name: Futsal Finder
earlier.summary: Tinder-style matchmaking for competitive futsal teams — teams set preferences and get paired with nearby opponents, with league and knockout tournaments, tiered battle seasons, and Airbnb-style court booking. My first end-to-end system.

aiEngineering.label: AI-ASSISTED ENGINEERING
aiEngineering.heading: The tools speed up the work. The judgment stays mine.
body: I use agentic coding tools to delegate work and then check it — a light model to explore, a stronger one to plan and design, a mid one to implement.
I read and test every change before it goes in, and if I don't understand a piece of code it doesn't merge. The tools speed up boilerplate and exploration. The design calls and the quality stay mine.

Nexus and Aroma were both built with spec-driven development: I write the spike, the reference implementation and the spec myself, then AI models plan and implement against the frozen spec. I read every change before it merges.
